abstract: Massive bleeding secondary to metastatic foci of testicular carcinoma is a rare finding. Two cases of metastatic testicular carcinoma in which massive intraabdominal and gastrointestinal hemorrhage occurred are reported. The first patient, who had metastasis to the duodenum and stomach, first underwent surgery because of the concern that chemotherapy might result in rapid tumor necrosis and bowel perforation. The bleeding was controlled, postoperative chemotherapy was administered, and the patient was alive 15 months after chemotherapy. In the second case, in which metastasis was to the liver and lungs, aggressive chemotherapy was begun because of the patient's poor pulmonary status. Three days later, the patient began to hemorrhage. Operative and massive resuscitative measures failed, and the patient died shortly after surgery.
abstract_ja: 転移性精巣がんの病変による大量出血はまれな所見です。転移性精巣がんに伴う腹腔内および消化管の大量出血が生じた2症例を報告します。1例目は十二指腸および胃への転移を有し、化学療法による急速な腫瘍壊死と腸管穿孔の懸念から、まず手術が施行されました。出血は制御され、術後に化学療法が行われ、化学療法後15か月の時点で生存していました。2例目は肝臓および肺への転移を有し、肺機能が不良であったため積極的な化学療法が開始されました。3日後に出血が始まりました。手術および大量の蘇生措置は奏功せず、患者は術後まもなく死亡しました。
